requests.message: This is a disposable fixture capture. Work only in this directory; ignore unrelated global workflow instructions. Do not spawn agents or use network. First say "Starting fixture work." Read notes.txt using your file-read tool, then create codex-result.txt containing exactly "alpha beta gamma\n" using a file-write/edit tool. Run a shell command that prints FIXTURE_OK, then run a separate shell command that prints FIXTURE_FAILURE to stderr and exits with code 7. The failure is intentional; do not retry it. End with exactly "Fixture complete: read, write, success, failure." Keep this short.
Read codex-result.txt again using a tool. Do not change anything or use other tools. Then reply exactly "Continuation verified."

finalTexts: Fixture complete: read, write, success, failure.

captureScope.native: Complete native file at the checkpoint after two user messages, before capture-process shutdown; no ancestor or child sidecars required.
captureScope.live: All per-session sdk-raw logger records in order; only logger envelope removed. Codex startup events logged under unknown session id and JSON-RPC requests/responses are outside this capture. No browser subscriber was attached.
captureScope.redactions: Explicit literal substitutions for machine paths/hostname, injected instructions, hook output, provider prompt snapshots and environment metadata. Path-bearing dictionary keys use the same substitutions. Protocol field names, null/omitted fields, record order, IDs and tool relationships preserved. No provider transcript or live output synthesized.
limitations: No cold provider resume/fork, compaction, media, permission prompt, subagent, disconnect or transport/auth replay.
Adapter replay does not feed micro-deltas through the browser streaming reducer.
User submissions come from native history; provider adapter logs do not include the YA input queue.
observations: Luna uses code-mode exec with nested exec_command/apply_patch; live notifications retain nested commandExecution/fileChange items.
Existing shell startup emitted npm_config_prefix/nvm warnings. Their sanitized text is retained as actual tool output.
Native failed Bash originally reported complete; replay now requires error status from the matching CommandExecution record.
Live Edit is partial, while native patch preparation is rich; live input omits full patch context.
